home.title: editonny — video editing through conversation
home.description: Editonny is a video editing skill for Codex and Claude Code, 100% free and open source. Cut pauses, caption, clean up audio, reframe, and create motion scenes by asking in plain language.

anatomy.lead: Pull the edit apart and see what each part of the request does. Put it back together and it becomes the video.
anatomy.plate1Text: The material as recorded: takes, breaths, pauses and repeats.
anatomy.plate2Text: Markers define what goes. Clips move closer and the rhythm shows up.
anatomy.plate3Text: Text follows the speech word by word, highlighting what matters.
anatomy.plate4Text: A piece of speech becomes a scene: list, comparison, number or diagram.

features.lead: You say what you want to say. Editor handles cutting and finishing; Motion turns parts of your speech into scenes.

cuts.title: Pause and mistake cuts
cuts.text: Removes hesitations and repeats without clipping words.

story.title: Storytelling
story.text: Picks the clearest takes and shapes a beginning, middle and end.

captions.title: Captions
captions.text: Synced to the speech, highlighting the important words.

audio.title: Audio adjustments
audio.text: Volume, voice and music balanced to sound right on a phone.

reframe.title: Reframing

lists.title: Animated lists
lists.text: Steps that land on the beat of your speech.

comparisons.title: Comparisons
comparisons.text: Before and after, this or that, side by side.

numbers.title: Numbers

lab.lead: Play with the controls and watch each request work. Use the same phrases in your Reels, ads and lessons.
lab.tokens: So…|pause 1.2 s|to edit a video|you need|uh,|three steps.|pause 0.8 s|First, record.|Then cut…|Then cut.|And publish.
lab.captionSample: every word on time with emphasis on what matters
lab.question: The question everyone always asks?
lab.answer: THE ANSWER, STRAIGHT TO THE POINT.
lab.footnote: Illustrative schematic. The real composition is rendered by the agent from your footage.
lab.cta: All of this is free and open source.

cut.input: A spoken recording with long pauses, a hesitation and a repeated sentence.
cut.request: Cut the pauses and mistakes without clipping words, keeping the expressive pauses.
cut.output: Continuous speech with rhythm. Words and meaning stay exactly as spoken.

captions.input: The same clip, already cut, with no text on screen.
captions.request: Add readable captions, highlighting the spoken word.
captions.output: Captions synced word by word. You choose the lettering style.

format.input: A video shot vertically, subject in the center.
format.request: Adapt the video to {format} keeping the face and subject in frame.
format.output: Reframing that keeps the subject. The AI checks the framing in the chosen format.

lab.motionOutput: The moment becomes a full-screen scene with the words from your speech. Captions step aside during the scene.

steps.label: Three steps
steps.request: When I list the method, turn the three steps into an animated composition.
steps.input: A moment where the speech sums up a three-step method.

beforeAfter.label: Before and after
beforeAfter.request: In the comparison, show how it was and how it turned out, with the two numbers I mention.
beforeAfter.input: A moment where the speech compares how it was and how it turned out.

number.label: Number spotlight
number.request: When I mention revenue, highlight the amount with a number scene.
number.input: A moment where the speech mentions revenue or a result in money.

question.label: Question and answer
question.request: When I answer the audience's question, show the question and the answer on screen.
question.input: A moment where the speech answers a common audience question.

how.lead: Editonny is a skill installed on your computer. This page doesn't receive or edit videos — it's the reference to discover features, learn the flow and write requests.
how.step1Text: The code is open and free. Download the ZIP or clone the repository.
how.step2Text: Open the folder in Claude Code or Codex and paste the install request. It does the rest.
how.step3Text: Call $editonny or /editonny, point to your video folder and ask. You review a sample before the full video.
how.needNote: The installer sets up the engine dependencies. System tools must be available in the terminal.
how.cost1Text: is free and open source. No subscription, no paid plan.
how.cost2Text: may require its own subscription, purchased separately.
how.cost3Text: run on your machine. No video is sent through this site.

guide.step2Title: Open the folder in your agent
guide.step1Text: Open the repository, click Code → Download ZIP and unzip it. Or clone it with git.
guide.step2Text: Open the Editonny folder in Claude Code or Codex — either works.
guide.step3Text: It installs or updates the skill globally, prepares the environment and validates it in Claude Code and Codex. End to end, on its own.
guide.step4Text: Open a new conversation and call /editonny in Claude Code or $editonny in Codex. Point to your video folder and ask for a sample.
guide.restart: Close and reopen your agent after installing so it discovers the skill.
guide.askLead: Works for a first install and for updates. Paste it with the Editonny folder open in your agent:
guide.installNote: No terminal commands. If the agent needs anything, it asks first.
guide.terminal: Prefer the terminal? See the installation commands
guide.faqFreeTitle: Is it really free? What runs locally?
guide.faqFreeBody: Yes. Editonny is 100% free and open source, with no paid plan. This site builds requests and browses the catalog; it doesn't upload or edit anything in the browser. Transcription and rendering run on your machine; your AI agent follows its provider's terms and may require its own subscription.
guide.faqCatalogTitle: Does the catalog work in any format?
guide.faqCatalogBody: Scenes show their source format, usually vertical. The AI adapts and checks framing when your video has another aspect ratio. A visual reference does not guarantee an identical render without review.

Install.lead: Editing and visual scenes together. A portable skill for Codex and Claude Code, running on your computer.
Install.step1Text: Download the repository and open a terminal in the folder containing install.py. Ask your AI to read skills/editonny/SKILL.md and its setup reference for the package's current requirements.
Install.step2Text: The installer shares one package between both agents. To use just one, replace both with codex or claude. Restart your agent afterward so it discovers the skill.
Install.step3Text: Complete setup prepares local tools, the renderer, browser, default transcription model, local OCR for caption checks, and bundled media. Verify them with diagnostics and a synthetic sample; report anything pending before editing.
Install.step4Text: Use $editonny in Codex or /editonny in Claude Code. Ask for a sample before the complete project.
Install.askTitle: Installation starts with a request too.
Install.askRequest: Install editonny from this repository for Codex and Claude Code. First read skills/editonny/SKILL.md and follow its complete setup procedure. Prepare the compatible local tools, locked engine, pinned renderer and browser, default transcription model, local OCR for caption checks, and bundled media before the first edit. Verify setup with diagnostics and a synthetic sample, preserve my settings, and report pending steps. Check GitHub updates on each use and ask before applying them. Ask before paid services or sending my media.
Install.copyFallback: Copying is unavailable here. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C or ⌘C.
Install.faq1Body: The installer registers one copy at ~/.local/share/editonny, with links at ~/.agents/skills/editonny for Codex and ~/.claude/skills/editonny for Claude Code. Choose one installation method.
Install.faq2Body: Run python3 install.py --target codex or python3 install.py --target claude, then start a new conversation. Registration is local: it does not sync tools or files with cloud sessions or your phone.
Install.faq3Body: The skill checks GitHub on each use and asks before applying updates. After acceptance, run the installer from the new checkout and repeat complete setup checks. The previous version moves to ~/.local/share/editonny-backups/ and installation .env files are preserved. Managed plugins use their host's updater. An unavailable update check does not block a working local installation. Keep footage and projects outside the skill folder, and check the update before deleting any backup.
Install.faq4Body: Run python3 install.py --target both --uninstall. Add --dry-run to see the destinations first. Only the agent links are removed; the shared package, settings, backups, videos, and projects stay.
Install.faq5Title: Load as a Claude Code plugin
Install.faq5Body: Run claude --plugin-dir "/path/to/editonny" to load this checkout for one session, then invoke /editonny:editonny. The standalone skill uses /editonny; avoid loading both at once. Video tools and the Python environment are still required.
Install.faq6Title: What runs locally? What costs money?
Install.faq6Body: This guide builds requests and browses examples and scenes. It does not upload or edit footage in the browser. Your agent may require a subscription. Optional external generators may charge fees; the default request asks for your authorization before using them or sending media.
Install.faq7Title: How do I review the first sample?
Install.faq7Body: Listen for clipped words, check caption accuracy, and see whether framing keeps the subject. Ask for changes before finishing everything.
